content:
maria_customer: Hey team — starting yesterday (~11:20 UTC) some of our users see chat responses cut off mid-sentence when we use the Hosted API over SSE. We reliably get the first few tokens, then a 20–40s pause, and sometimes the final chunk never arrives. We surface X-Request-ID: req_8f3a2c9b in our app logs. Using eu-west-1, model=redwood-14b-v1.

jordan_support: Thanks Maria — sorry you're hitting this. Can you share a minimal curl repro and the exact SSE payloads you see? Also confirm if you have any edge proxy (Cloudflare, Fastly) or an internal gateway in front of us.

maria_customer: Repro curl below (we're using Cloudflare Workers in front, yes). Observed SSE stream (truncated):

```
curl -N -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_KEY" -H "Accept: text/event-stream" \
  "https://api.redwood.example/v1/chat.stream?model=redwood-14b-v1&session=sess-1204"
```

Observed events we logged client-side (timestamps removed):
```
event: message
data: {"delta":"Hello, here'"}

[no data for ~30s]

event: message
data: {"delta":"s how we can help."}
```

maria_customer: We also collected the proxy trace showing a 504 from the edge at 11:20:39 and then a reconnect. No errors from our backend.

sam_sre: Pls attach the full debug bundle (curl -v trace, tcpdump or ngrep if possible) and the edge trace. Also confirm whether this only happens on SSE vs websocket.

maria_customer: Attaching small bundle: curl verbose (headers only) + Fastly trace snippet.

```
# curl -v (headers)
* Connected to api.redwood.example (52.17.34.9) port 443 (#0)
> GET /v1/chat.stream?model=redwood-14b-v1&session=sess-1204 HTTP/1.1
> Host: api.redwood.example
> Accept: text/event-stream
> Authorization: Bearer REDACTED
> User-Agent: curl/7.88.1
>
< HTTP/1.1 200 OK
< Content-Type: text/event-stream; charset=utf-8
< Transfer-Encoding: chunked
< X-Request-ID: req_8f3a2c9b
< Server-Timing: edge;dur=30,proxy;dur=301
```

Fastly trace (snip):
```
11:20:35 client -> fastly (established)
11:20:36 fastly -> origin (established)
11:20:36 origin -> fastly (200 OK)
11:20:36 fastly -> client (first chunk)
11:21:06 fastly -> client (connection idle; no data forwarded; 504 sent)
11:21:07 client -> fastly (reconnect)
```

meera_oncall: Looks like the edge sent a 504 after ~30s of inactivity. Two questions: 1) Did Redwood send any keepalive comments or pings? 2) Do you have a backend proxy config that drops idle streaming connections?

jordan_support: On our side: request req_8f3a2c9b shows streaming tokens generated from 11:20:36to 11:21:20 with regular small writes at ~1s cadence. There is a gap in our logs between 11:20:58 and 11:21:12 but our writer shows no TCP close. We do write occasional comment lines like `: keepalive` every 15s for long requests, but for short chat sessions we don't if the model finishes quickly.

sam_sre: Two hypotheses: (A) Fastly idle timeout is 30s and swallowed late tokens because the client/proxy didn't see data for >30s; or (B) Cloudflare Workers buffering aggregated small chunks and then nothing reaching the client until a flush or timeout. We need a clean websocket vs SSE comparison and a direct curl from their origin (bypassing Fastly) to validate.

maria_customer: Quick test results:
- Direct curl to api.redwood.example from an EC2 in eu-west-1 (no fastly) shows steady SSE events every 900-1200ms, completes fine.
- Through Cloudflare Worker (same region) we see the partial output behavior.

maria_customer: Repro steps to reproduce from our side (we included the worker script):
1) Deploy Worker that proxies request and does `response = await fetch(apiUrl, {headers})` and returns response body as-is.
2) Start chat call from browser -> worker -> Redwood (SSE).
3) Observe first ~10 tokens, then pause, then sometimes final chunk missing.

worker snippet:
```
addEventListener('fetch', event => {
  event.respondWith(handle(event.request))
})

async function handle(req) {
  const apiUrl = 'https://api.redwood.example' + new URL(req.url).pathname + new URL(req.url).search
  const headers = { 'Authorization': 'Bearer ' + REDACTED, 'Accept': 'text/event-stream' }
  const res = await fetch(apiUrl, { headers })
  return new Response(res.body, { headers: { 'Content-Type': 'text/event-stream' } })
}
```

meera_oncall: Can you add manual keepalive comments from the worker into the proxied stream (e.g., write `: keepalive\n\n` every 10s) and see if that prevents Fastly from timing out? Also try websocket proxying (if Workers support) to see if it avoids the issue.

sam_sre: Also request the full nginx/edge config for the customer's origin if they have one, and the worker runtime timeout settings. If this clear repro, we can add optional keepalive comments from our end for SSE when we detect edge proxies.

jordan_support: Next steps for customer: 1) confirm Worker keepalive test, 2) try websocket via worker, 3) gather ngrep/tcpdump if still failing. For Redwood: we will check for any write stalls in our runtime and consider emitting `: keepalive` every 10s for streams longer than 10s.

maria_customer: Will run tests and report back. Thanks all :thumbsup:
